text:
Recent work supports separating sampling coverage from optimization bias. [Improved Estimation of Ranks (2024)](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) shows that sampled negatives bias rank estimates; large sampled margins therefore cannot establish good catalog ranks. [Sequential negative-sampling experiments (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find sampler-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) revisits sampled-softmax gradients when positives are included deterministically. These results motivate measuring the actual competing items and gradient directions before changing the loss.

Suggested diagnostic, inferred from this literature: freeze the single NextItNet and use training-only prefix/next-item examples with identical candidate eligibility. Record exact eligible-catalog target rank, sampled rank, and the fraction of target-outranking items covered by sampled negatives. Also measure captured catalog softmax probability mass. Compare sampled-loss versus catalog-softmax gradients using cosine similarity and relative error, separately for sequence features, item embeddings, and backbone parameters; report high-scoring competitors with opposing gradient contributions. Catalog softmax is a diagnostic reference objective, not ground-truth relevance supervision.

For dot-product scores, decompose each competitor margin using s(h,i)=||h||||e_i||cos(h,e_i). Report embedding norms, angular similarities, training popularity, and rank changes under diagnostic-only item normalization. This separates magnitude-associated failures from angular misalignment, although normalization cannot prove causality. [Sampled-softmax analysis (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) warns that overly hard negatives can dominate gradients; [PSL (2024)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/db1d5c63576587fc1d40d33a75190c71-Abstract-Conference.html) highlights false-negative sensitivity. Keep normalization and catalog probes diagnostic-only, preserve final-nonpadding readout, and leave the pinned evaluator unchanged.
